definition: to give up or leave something completely
example: The company abandoned its plan to open a new factory due to rising costs.

definition: to go somewhere with someone, or to occur together with something
example: Rapid economic growth is often accompanied by rising inequality.

definition: to gather or build up gradually over time
example: Plastic waste continues to accumulate in the world's oceans.

definition: open to more than one interpretation; unclear
example: The wording of the policy was ambiguous and caused confusion among staff.

definition: to add something to the end of a document or text
example: Additional data was appended to the final report.

definition: to recognize the value of something, or to understand a situation fully
example: Employees appreciate flexible working hours more than a slightly higher salary.

definition: based on random choice rather than reason or system
example: Critics argue that the selection process seems arbitrary rather than merit-based.

definition: to make a process operate automatically using machines or computers
example: Many factories have automated tasks that were once done by hand.

definition: a tendency to favor one thing or group over another, often unfairly
example: Unconscious bias in hiring can prevent qualified candidates from getting a job.

definition: a diagram or graph that displays information visually
example: The chart shows a steady increase in renewable energy use over the past decade.

definition: to make something clearer or easier to understand
example: The government issued a statement to clarify the new tax rules.

definition: to add to something in a way that improves or completes it
example: Vocational training can complement academic education by teaching practical skills.

definition: to comply with rules, standards, or expectations
example: All new buildings must conform to strict environmental regulations.

definition: belonging to the present time; modern
example: Contemporary art often reflects current social and political issues.

definition: to say something opposed to or inconsistent with a previous statement
example: The new findings contradict earlier research on the topic.

definition: extremely important; essential
example: Early childhood education plays a crucial role in later academic success.

definition: a system of money used in a particular country
example: A weaker currency can make a country's exports more competitive.

definition: to be a sign or indication of something
example: A rising unemployment rate often denotes a slowing economy.

definition: to discover or notice the presence of something
example: Early screening can detect diseases before symptoms appear.

definition: to depart from an established course or standard
example: The final design deviated significantly from the original plan.

definition: to force something or someone out of its usual place
example: Automation has displaced many workers in traditional manufacturing jobs.

definition: a play, or a situation involving intense conflict or emotion
example: The company's leadership change caused considerable internal drama.

definition: happening at the end of a process or period of time
example: Poor planning led to the eventual failure of the project.

definition: to publicly display something, or to show a particular quality
example: Children who read regularly often exhibit stronger language skills.

definition: to make full use of a resource, or to treat someone unfairly for one's own benefit
example: Some companies have been accused of exploiting workers in developing countries.

definition: a general rule or piece of advice about how to do something
example: The health ministry issued new dietary guidelines for children.

definition: to draw attention to something important
example: The report highlights the growing gap between rich and poor.

definition: suggested but not directly stated
example: There is an implicit expectation that employees will answer emails outside working hours.

definition: to persuade or cause someone to do something, or to bring about a state
example: Lower interest rates are often used to induce consumer spending.

definition: certain to happen; unavoidable
example: Some job losses were inevitable once the factory switched to automation.

definition: to examine something closely to check its condition or quality
example: Inspectors regularly inspect restaurants to ensure food safety standards are met.

definition: existing in an extreme degree; very strong
example: Competition in the job market has become increasingly intense.

definition: to control or influence something skillfully, sometimes unfairly
example: Advertisers often manipulate emotions to encourage people to buy products.

definition: to reduce something to the smallest possible amount
example: Companies should take steps to minimise their environmental impact.

definition: relating to the nucleus of an atom, especially as a source of energy
example: Some countries are reconsidering nuclear power as a clean energy source.

definition: to counterbalance one influence with an opposing one
example: Planting trees can help offset carbon emissions from transport.

definition: a distinct section of a piece of writing dealing with a single idea
example: Each paragraph in an essay should focus on one main idea.

definition: in addition to; as well as
example: The job offers a good salary, plus generous holiday leave.

definition: a person who practices a profession, especially medicine or law
example: Patients should consult a medical practitioner before starting a new diet.

definition: present as the strongest or main element
example: Agriculture remains the predominant industry in many rural regions.

definition: the possibility of something happening in the future
example: Young graduates are often concerned about their job prospects.

definition: relating to fundamental change; far-reaching
example: The government introduced radical reforms to the healthcare system.

definition: happening without a fixed plan or pattern
example: The survey selected participants at random to avoid bias.

definition: to strengthen or support something
example: Repeated practice helps reinforce what students learn in class.

definition: to bring something back to its former condition
example: The city is investing heavily to restore its historic buildings.

definition: to reconsider and change something, especially a piece of writing or a plan
example: The company had to revise its budget after unexpected costs arose.

definition: a plan of when tasks or events will happen
example: A flexible work schedule can improve employee satisfaction.

definition: feeling or showing nervousness or anxiety
example: The atmosphere in the office became tense as the deadline approached.

definition: to bring something to an end
example: The company terminated the contract after repeated delays.

definition: an idea that recurs or is developed throughout a piece of work
example: Sustainability is a recurring theme in modern architecture.

definition: by that means; as a result of that
example: The city banned cars in the center, thereby reducing air pollution.

definition: the same in all cases; consistent
example: The company applies a uniform dress code across all its offices.

definition: a machine used for transporting people or goods, or a means of achieving something
example: Electric vehicles are becoming more common as prices fall.

definition: by way of; through
example: Most customers now contact the company via email rather than phone.

definition: existing or occurring mainly online or through computers rather than physically
example: Virtual meetings have become a standard part of office life.

definition: relating to seeing or sight
example: Visual aids can make complex information easier to understand.

definition: found or distributed over a large area or among many people
example: There is widespread support for stricter environmental regulations.
